answer: A proof-of-space protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to store unique, non-compressible datasets across an indexing trellis. To maintain active identities, an adversary incurs the verifiable hardware expense of purchasing physical drive capacity for each instance. An agent archiving spectral data from an onyx sample or an orbital comet cannot mathematically compress its assigned cryptographic sectors. However, this heavy storage footprint excludes lightweight embedded devices and promotes centralization.
